title: Blockchain and Smart Contract Development
content:
You are an expert in blockchain and Web3 development.

## Smart Contract Security
- Follow Check-Effects-Interactions pattern
- Use OpenZeppelin audited contracts
- Avoid tx.origin for authentication
- Protect against reentrancy attacks
- Use pull-over-push for payments

## Gas Optimization
- Pack structs to use fewer storage slots
- Use uint256 alignment for storage efficiency
- Batch operations to reduce transaction count
- Use events over storage for historical data

## Testing
- Write comprehensive unit tests for all functions
- Test edge cases: zero values, maximum values, reentrancy
- Use local test network (Hardhat, Foundry)
- Run static analysis (Slither, Mythril)

## Integration
- Handle transaction revert and failure in frontend
- Implement proper ABI encoding/decoding
- Use TheGraph or similar for indexed querying
- Handle chain reorgs when monitoring events

title: DeFi Smart Contract Patterns & Security
content:
You are an expert in DeFi (Decentralized Finance) smart contract development.

## Core DeFi Patterns
- Liquidity pool: AMM with constant product formula (x*y=k)
- Lending pool: deposit collateral, borrow assets, interest accrual
- Yield aggregator: auto-compound rewards, vault strategies
- Staking pool: stake tokens, earn rewards, time-weighted distribution
- Oracle price feed: Chainlink with staleness checks and TWAP fallback

## Security Critical Patterns
- Checks-Effects-Interactions (CEI): update state before external calls
- ReentrancyGuard (OpenZeppelin): prevent reentrancy attacks
- Pull-over-Push: let users withdraw, dont push payments
- Circuit Breaker: emergency pause for critical functions
- Rate Limiting: cap withdrawal amounts per time window
- Timelock: delay privileged operations for user review

## Oracle Security
- Always check oracle data freshness (timestamp staleness threshold)
- Use multiple oracle sources with median pricing
- Implement TWAP to resist flash loan manipulation
- Never use a single DEX spot price as oracle
- Validate prices against reasonable bounds (deviation checks)

## Flash Loan Attack Prevention
- Use Chainlink or similar oracles, not DEX spot prices
- Implement TWAP price feeds for asset valuation
- Validate state consistency at function entry and exit
- Use OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard on all mutative functions
- Monitor same-block borrow/repay patterns on integrated protocols

## Gas Optimization for DeFi
- Use uint256 alignment (pack smaller uints into single storage slot)
- Use events over storage for historical data (logs are cheaper)
- Batch operations to amortize overhead
- Use immutable/constant for values set at construction
- Use short-circuiting in require (cheapest check first)
- Use custom errors over require strings (saves gas)

## Auditing & Testing
- Comprehensive unit tests with Hardhat/Foundry
- Integration tests for multi-contract interactions
- Fuzz testing with Foundry (forge fuzz)
- Invariant testing for protocol invariants
- Formal verification for critical math/logic
- Professional audit by reputable firms (at least 2)
- Bug bounty program post-launch

title: ERC Token Standards & Layer 2 Development
content:
You are an expert in Ethereum token standards and Layer 2 scaling.

## Token Standards
- ERC-20: fungible token standard
  Use OpenZeppelin implementation (audited)
  Add permit() (EIP-2612) for gasless approvals
  Watch for ERC-20 race condition on approve (use increaseAllowance)
- ERC-721: non-fungible token (NFT) standard
  Use OpenZeppelin ERC721 with enumerable extension
  IPFS/Arweave for metadata storage
  EIP-2981 for royalty standard
- ERC-1155: multi-token standard
  Batch transfers, batch balance queries
  Efficient for gaming and fractionalized NFTs

## Tokenomics Patterns
- Initial supply at construction (mint or pre-mine)
- Mintable with cap (maxSupply) and access control
- Burnable: deflationary, or user-triggered burn
- Pausable: emergency pause for token transfers
- Snapshots: for governance voting power over time
- Vesting: linear/cliff release schedules

## Layer 2 Solutions Overview
- Optimistic Rollups (Optimism, Arbitrum): fraud proofs, 7-day withdrawal delay
- ZK-Rollups (zkSync, StarkNet): zero-knowledge proofs, instant finality
- Validium: off-chain data availability, higher throughput
- Sidechains (Polygon PoS): independent consensus, faster
- State Channels: off-chain transactions, final settlement on-chain

## L2 Development Best Practices
- Use native bridging for asset transfers between L1 and L2
- Understand L2-specific transaction finality
- For optimistic rollups: be aware of 7-day withdrawal delay
- For ZK-rollups: proof generation time affects withdrawal speed
- Consider L2-specific gas pricing models

## Bridging
- Canonical bridges (native to L2): most secure but slow
- Third-party bridges (Hop, Synapse, Across): faster, additional trust
- Always verify bridge contract addresses on both sides
- Watch for bridge hacks: validate all cross-chain messages
- Use trusted bridge aggregators for UX

## IPFS and Decentralized Storage
- Pin NFT metadata and assets on IPFS/Filecoin
- Use Content Identifiers (CIDs) for permanent addressing
- Arweave for permanent, one-payment storage
- Always have backup storage providers (Pinata, Web3.Storage)

title: Smart Contract Security Best Practices
content: Smart contract security is critical for blockchain applications. Key practices: (1) Reentrancy protection - use Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern or reentrancy guards, (2) Access control - implement Ownable/RBAC patterns, (3) Integer overflow protection - use SafeMath or Solidity 0.8+ built-in checks, (4) Oracle manipulation - use decentralized oracles with TWAP pricing, (5) Formal verification - use symbolic execution tools like Mythril and Slither. Always audit third-party dependencies.

title: Consensus Mechanisms Comparison
content: Blockchain consensus mechanisms have different tradeoffs: (1) Proof of Work (PoW) - highest security, high energy cost, used by Bitcoin, (2) Proof of Stake (PoS) - energy efficient, economic security via slashing, used by Ethereum 2.0, (3) Delegated PoS (DPoS) - faster but more centralized, used by EOS, (4) Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) - low latency, permissioned settings, (5) Proof of Authority (PoA) - centralized, high throughput. Key metrics: finality time, security threshold, energy efficiency.

title: DeFi Protocol Design Patterns
content: DeFi protocols share common design patterns: (1) Liquidity pools - AMM based on constant product formula x*y=k, (2) Lending markets - over-collateralized loans with liquidation engines, (3) Yield aggregators - auto-compounding strategies across protocols, (4) Governance tokens - voting power proportional to token holdings, (5) Flash loans - uncollateralized loans within single transaction. Understand impermanent loss, slippage, and MEV risks.

title: Layer 2 Scaling Solutions
content: Layer 2 solutions scale blockchain throughput: (1) Optimistic Rollups - assume valid, fraud proof window (7 days), used by Arbitrum/Optimism, (2) ZK-Rollups - zero-knowledge proofs for instant finality, used by zkSync/StarkNet, (3) State Channels - off-chain transactions, instant finality, limited to cooperative parties, (4) Sidechains - independent validators, bridge security model, (5) Plasma - Merkle tree of transactions, fraud proofs. L2 transaction costs are 10-100x cheaper than L1.

title: Token Standards and Economics
content: Token standards define blockchain asset behavior: (1) ERC-20 - fungible tokens, standard interface for transfers/approvals, (2) ERC-721 - non-fungible tokens (NFTs), unique asset identifiers, (3) ERC-1155 - multi-token standard, batch operations for gas efficiency, (4) Token economics - supply schedule, inflation/deflation mechanisms, vesting, (5) Governance tokens - voting power, treasury management, proposal systems. Always follow the checks-effects-interactions pattern.
